headline: High: shared-workspace Notion AI can leak workspace content into a broad-network Open WebUI pair, with default interaction paths also enabling prompt injection and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI ingests workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while Open WebUI supports MCP, plugins, and tool servers. If Notion content is copied or synced into Open WebUI, attacker-controlled text can steer tool use. The pair lacks documented provenance isolation, so the interaction is plausible though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Notion page content is transferred into Open WebUI prompts or files without provenance tagging, injection is possible.
IF Open WebUI tool calls are enabled for content originating from Notion, instructions embedded in that content can be followed.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Notion exports into Open WebUI prompts.
Add a manual review step before any Notion-derived text reaches tool-enabled chats.
Prefix imported content with a non-executable provenance banner.
Restrict Open WebUI tools for chats that reference workspace content.
requires-engineering: add content provenance labels and instruction-stripping filters.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, and Open WebUI handles local files, mounted volumes, API keys, and broad network egress. If the pair shares a workspace or copied documents, sensitive workspace data can flow into Open WebUI and then out through its external APIs. The blast radius includes exfiltration and secrets exposure.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem, mounted volume, or copied documents, workspace content can be exposed to Open WebUI.
IF Open WebUI is configured with external API providers, any imported sensitive content can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep Notion exports out of Open WebUI's mounted data volume.
Remove unused external API providers from Open WebUI.
Rotate any API keys stored in Open WebUI before importing workspace data.
Use separate OS accounts or containers for each agent.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data loss prevention and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Notion AI has shared workspace state across instances, and Open WebUI uses persistent shared web-app sessions with Redis-backed multi-worker state. Both can mutate shared content, so concurrent edits or writes can conflict if they target the same documents or synced artifacts. The profiles do not show locking between them.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same synced document or mounted volume, last-write-wins conflicts can occur.
IF Open WebUI sessions are shared across workers while Notion content is mirrored, concurrent updates can diverge.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory or sync target.
Pause one agent while the other performs writes to shared artifacts.
Use file-level locks on any mirrored documents.
Review and reconcile diffs before publishing changes.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, and Open WebUI supports tool use and persistent sessions. If Notion output is treated as authoritative by Open WebUI, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream actions or generated artifacts. The pair lacks a built-in verification step in the profiles.
conditions: IF Open WebUI consumes Notion answers without verification, incorrect facts can propagate into later chats or tool calls.
IF Open WebUI is allowed to act on Notion-generated summaries, downstream outputs may encode the same error.
mitigations: Require source links for any Notion-derived claim before reuse.
Add a human verification step before tool execution in Open WebUI.
Limit Open WebUI to drafting only for Notion-sourced content.
Flag low-confidence Notion answers for review.
requires-engineering: implement citation checking and confidence gating between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI is vendor-hosted and workspace-scoped, while Open WebUI can run with broad network egress and handle API keys, local files, and mounted volumes. If regulated workspace content is moved from Notion into Open WebUI, retention and residency controls can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer assumption is a policy mismatch risk.
conditions: IF regulated data from Notion is copied into Open WebUI, retention and logging policies may differ.
IF Open WebUI is connected to third-party APIs, residency constraints on workspace content may be violated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Open WebUI chats and files.
Disable third-party providers for compliance-sensitive sessions.
Document retention settings for both systems before use.
Separate EU or PHI workloads from general-purpose Open WebUI usage.
requires-engineering: align residency, retention, and deletion workflows across both systems.
